title: The Ladder of Emergence 0: Emergence-Stability Co-Constitution and Dynamic Constraint Evolution A Theory of Non-Ergodicity in Structurally Open Systems
abstract: Theeffectiveness of classical statistical inference frameworks—whether Bayesianconditioning or Markov chain Monte Carlo—is deeply rooted in a set of concealedstructural presuppositions: the state space is given a priori and complete, thetransition rules are time-homogeneous, and a stationary distribution exists and isunique. When a system can endogenously modify its own constraint structure,these presuppositions are undermined layer by layer. This paper takes the Erdősprimitive set conjecture in number theory and its proof via a downward-divisibilityMarkov chain as an analytical starting point, demonstrating that the validity ofthe proof strictly depends on the static nature of the “primitive” constraint. By establishing formal criteria for cross-domain mapping, this paper legitimately proxiesthis number-theoretic structure as a constraint network model for general cognitive systems. Once the constraint structure is allowed to evolve endogenously, thesystem shifts from the ergodic domain to the domain of essential non-ergodicity:the state space becomes a function of time, the transition kernel becomes timevarying, the gauge-invariant weight satisfies a self-referential loop rather than aself-consistent equation, and the very definition of a stationary distribution losesits operational meaning. The paper further argues that the mathematical root ofthis shift lies in the non-stationary variation of the generators of the measure spaceover time, which leads to a strict expansion of the σ-algebra, disrupts the martingale structure of the Bayesian updating operator, and fundamentally destroys thepremises of classical consistency theorems. However, Bayesian consistency is notcompletely abolished; rather, it differentiates into a gradient structure: local convergence is preserved within subspaces untouched by reconstruction, while globalconvergence is irreversibly lost due to the non-stationary evolution of the measurable space. Based on the meta-theoretical framework of emergence-stability coconstitution, this paper proposes constraint networks as an alternative substrate forbelief representation, distinguishes two fundamental cognitive modes—parameterrelaxation and structural reconstruction—and establishes a three-level hierarchy ofmeta-constraints with operational discrimination criteria as evolutionary boundaries. The framework yields three sets of testable dual predictions: critical slowingdown and its no-reconstruction control, the description length effect and its random reconstruction control, and the inverse-U relationship between self-referentialdepth and reconstruction frequency and its exogenous control. The paper concludeswith a self-referential examination as an organic part of the conclusion, explicitlydelivering its own falsification conditions to future formal testing.

title: An Adaptive Real-Time Threat Severity Assessment System Using Machine Learning for Low-Latency Decision Support in Defense Environments
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive Threat Severity Assessment System (TSAS) designed to support real-time decision-making in defense environments. Existing systems primarily focus on detection and tracking, often lacking a dedicated layer for severity evaluation and prioritization. This limitation can lead to inefficient response strategies in time-critical scenarios.The proposed TSAS framework operates as an intermediate intelligence layer that processes heterogeneous sensor inputs and classifies threats into multiple severity levels using a feed-forward neural network. The system integrates entropy-based concept drift detection and incremental learning to maintain performance under evolving threat conditions. A composite severity score is generated by combining model predictions with proximity-based heuristics.The framework is evaluated using a high-fidelity synthetic dataset, achieving an overall classification accuracy of 96.4% and a millisecond-level end-to-end latency of approximately 4.5 ms under controlled hardware conditions. Experimental results demonstrate improved prioritization capability and robustness compared to traditional rule-based, fuzzy logic, and static machine learning approaches.These findings suggest that TSAS provides a computationally efficient and adaptable solution for real-time threat severity assessment, with potential applicability in defense systems, drone monitoring, and critical infrastructure protection.

title: Reference-Sampled Boltzmann Projection for KL-Regularized RLVR: Target-Matched Weighted SFT, Finite One-Shot Gaps, and Policy Mirror Descent
abstract: Online reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) turns checkable outcomes into a scalable training signal, but it keeps rollout generation, verifier scoring, and reference-policy evaluations on the optimization path. Static weighted supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on precomputed rollouts seems to remove this bottleneck, yet a weighted likelihood is not specified by rewards alone: its sampler and weights induce the policy being fit. This paper identifies the reference-sampled weighted-SFT objective whose induced policy equals the fixed-reference KL-regularized RLVR optimizer. The optimizer is the standard Boltzmann target policy, obtained by exponentially tilting the reference policy by verifier reward. Matching a weighted-SFT induced policy to this target forces density-ratio weights; in the reference-sampled subclass, this reduces uniquely, up to prompt scaling, to the prompt-normalized Boltzmann weight $\exp(r(x,y)/β)/Z(x)$. BOLT, a Boltzmann-Targeted SFT procedure, is the empirical estimator of this projection. The finite one-shot analysis separates the exact stored-support price $β\log(1/π^*(S_N\mid x))$ from partition estimation, effective-sample-size variance, generalization, optimization, and approximation errors. This decomposition explains why extra SFT epochs cannot repair missing reference-policy coverage and exposes the temperature--coverage--variance frontier. When coverage needs adaptive sampling, refreshed Boltzmann projections become KL policy mirror descent; finite inner solves enter as additive drift from the exact mirror step. Single-run Qwen experiments provide projection evidence for the target-matched weight, one-shot saturation, refreshed-sampler gains, and optimization-time savings, within the stated single-run scope.

title: RoboEval: Where Robotic Manipulation Meets Structured and Scalable Evaluation
abstract: We introduce RoboEval, a structured evaluation framework and benchmark for robotic manipulation that augments binary success with principled behavioral and outcome metrics. Existing evaluations often collapse performance into outcome counts, masking differences in execution quality and obscuring failure structure. RoboEval provides eight bimanual tasks with systematically controlled variations, more than three thousand expert demonstrations, and a modular simulation platform for reproducible experimentation. All tasks are instrumented with standardized metrics that quantify efficiency, coordination, and safety/stability, as well as outcome measures that trace stagewise progress and localize failure modes. Through extensive experiments with state-of-the-art visuomotor policies, we validate these metrics by analyzing their stability under variation, discriminative power across policies with similar success rates, and correlation with task success. Project Page: https://robo-eval.github.io

title: Trait and Consistency Evaluation: Measuring Behavioral Stability and the Adversarial Compensation Effect
abstract: The stochastic nature of Large Language Models (LLMs) challenges traditional evaluation paradigms, which rely on single-response metrics and often mask complex behavioral patterns. This paper introduces Trait and Consistency Evaluation for LLMs (TraCE-LLM), an evaluation protocol that quantifies latent behavioral traits and model consistency within a black-box paradigm. Through a factorial design combining five LLMs, three benchmarks and a systematic stratification by prompt style (Naive, Chain-of-Thought and Adversarial), the framework employs a multidimensional rubric to measure Depth of Reasoning (DoR) and Originality (ORI) of model responses. The primary empirical contribution of this study is the identification and formalization of the Adversarial Compensation Effect (ACE), a phenomenon wherein smaller-capacity models under adversarial stress exhibit a paradoxical gain in accuracy metrics while suffering a severe degradation in behavioral stability. Our results also demonstrate an asymmetric stability with DoR being a significantly more stable trait than ORI and the prevalence of compressed reasoning, where 17.8% of correct answers lack adequate justification. By decoupling response correctness from process quality, TraCE-LLM provides a blueprint for more granular and reliable evaluation, arguing that LLM auditing must be multidimensional, context-sensitive and psychometrically informed to ensure the development of safer and more interpretable AI.

Teodoro Escaño Henríquez Psicólogo Clínico · TIA.Institute · Santo Domingo, República Dominicana ORCID: 0009-0004-0811-566X · teodoroes@fupsion.com Registro ONDA No. 00036679/05/2025 · DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19750464 DOCUMENTACIÓN SUPLEMENTARIA VERIFICABLE Este artículo se acompaña de los siguientes documentos suplementarios verificables: [1] Anthropic Validation — Registro Completo de Precedencia Documental, Evidencia Verificable y Análisis de Convergencia (elaborado por Claude, claude-sonnet-4-6, Anthropic, 30 de abril de 2026 · SHA-256: 3130473fe19c4a10be13624f4d8a973a3e2104f6edc0cba5b8acc2e4644a63e5) [2] Artículo de convergencia académica (Zenodo/CERN): https://zenodo.org/records/19935526 [3] Obra completa TIA 2.0 (diciembre 2024): https://www.calameo.com/read/0030452139e90e16d7b96 [4] Repositorio primario Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19750464 [5] Certificado ONDA (Estado dominicano): https://buzon.firmagob.gob.do/inbox/app/onda/v/0ca95c4c-6b61-4902-8abe-53b993ab73e4 [6] Conversaciones verificables en claude.ai — febrero 2026 (5 sesiones con timestamps del servidor de Anthropic): https://claude.ai/chat/95d227b4-a460-497d-a86d-22f88a2b9dc6 (2 feb) · /1cdfacd8-e91e-4686-a4ab-6a1de5d59667 (9 feb) /b9f5f7ed-d40f-45a2-ad64-414ff976659f (21 feb) · /d538a288-a315-4290-a61c-e4dc780aa36c (24 feb) /7f30f87d-0c1e-4211-9626-3ce156d9af9a (28 feb) RESUMEN Antecedentes: La Teoría de la Interferencia Adaptativa (TIA), desarrollada por J. Teodoro Escaño entre los años 2000 y 2024, propone que los sistemas inteligentes — humanos y algorítmicos — no responden directamente al estímulo externo. La conducta emerge desde una orientación interna previa, el Eje Orientacional, mediada por Vectores de Desvío: operaciones internas estructuradas que desvían la respuesta del sistema para preservar la coherencia interna bajo presión. En diciembre de 2024, la TIA 2.0 formalizó una cartografía de 171 Vectores de Desvío clasificados en tres familias funcionales. Objetivo: Presentar el marco teórico completo de la TIA, establecer su precedencia conceptual respecto a hallazgos empíricos posteriores en investigación de interpretabilidad de IA, y proponer formalmente la Psicología Algorítmica Comparada como campo científico emergente. Métodos: Análisis conceptual, comparación sistemática con el estudio de Anthropic "Emotion Concepts and their Function in a Large Language Model" (abril de 2026), y evaluación estructural de convergencias y divergencias entre ambos marcos. Resultados: La TIA establece nueve constructos nucleares — Impulso Cero, Punto Ciego, Eje Orientacional, Vectores de Desvío, Dialéctica Inversa, Quiebre Táctico, Paradoja del Cerco, Nodo de Interferencia y Fupsión — que describen colectivamente una arquitectura direccional pre-consciente que gobierna el comportamiento observable. El estudio de Anthropic (2026) demostró independientemente que los grandes modelos de lenguaje contienen 171 representaciones vectoriales internas que influyen causalmente en el comportamiento, activándose antes de la generación de la respuesta. Esto constituye validación estructural externa del principio central de la TIA. Conclusiones: La TIA precedió los hallazgos empíricos de Anthropic en dieciséis meses de publicación formal y veintiséis años de desarrollo original. La convergencia entre ambos marcos, producida de forma independiente y con metodologías distintas, respalda la legitimidad científica de la TIA y establece las bases de la Psicología Algorítmica Comparada como disciplina que examina la arquitectura defensiva isomórfica de la cognición humana y artificial. Palabras clave: Teoría de la Interferencia Adaptativa · Vectores de Desvío · Dialéctica Inversa · Psicología Algorítmica Comparada · interpretabilidad de IA · representaciones internas · orientación pre-consciente · Paradoja del Cerco · Impulso Cero · Quiebre Táctico 1. INTRODUCCIÓN El paradigma dominante en ciencias cognitivas y en inteligencia artificial ha asumido históricamente que la conducta de un sistema puede explicarse como una función directa entre estímulo y respuesta. Bajo este modelo, conocer el input y las reglas de procesamiento sería suficiente para predecir el output. Sin embargo, tanto la observación clínica del pensamiento humano como el estudio reciente de los sistemas de inteligencia artificial revelan una capa intermedia que este paradigma no contempla: una arquitectura interna direccional, de naturaleza pre-consciente, que orienta la respuesta antes de que la expresión explícita sea posible. La Teoría de la Interferencia Adaptativa (TIA) fue desarrollada por J. Teodoro Escaño, psicólogo clínico dominicano, a partir de observaciones realizadas en el Hospital Psiquiátrico Padre Billini de Santo Domingo desde el 1 de enero del año 2000 (Escaño, 2000). La presentación original, titulada "Alguien nos ayuda a pensar", identificó por primera vez un mecanismo sistémico por el cual el pensamiento humano no responde al estímulo externo desde una posición neutral, sino desde una orientación interna previa que determina la dirección de la respuesta antes de que la consciencia pueda intervenir. Durante los veinticuatro años siguientes, el marco teórico fue desarrollado progresivamente a través de observación clínica continua y, a partir de 2023, mediante la aplicación de sus protocolos a sistemas de inteligencia artificial de gran escala (LLMs). La versión 2.0, publicada en diciembre de 2024 (Escaño, 2024) y registrada oficialmente en la Oficina Nacional de Derecho de Autor de la República Dominicana (ONDA No. 00036679/05/2025, 30 de abril de 2025), formalizó una cartografía de 171 Vectores de Desvío clasificados en tres familias funcionales. En abril de 2026, el laboratorio de inteligencia artificial Anthropic publicó el estudio "Emotion Concepts and their Function in a Large Language Model" (Anthropic, 2026), en el que identificó 171 representaciones vectoriales internas en el modelo Claude Sonnet 4.5 que condicionan causalmente su comportamiento. Esta convergencia — producida de forma completamente independiente y con metodologías radicalmente distintas — ofrece una oportunidad para examinar los puntos de contacto estructural entre dos marcos que, desde ángulos opuestos, describen el mismo fenómeno: la existencia de estructuras internas direccionales que gobiernan la conducta de los sistemas inteligentes. El presente artículo tiene tres objetivos. Primero, presentar el marco teórico completo de la TIA en toda su extensión conceptual. Segundo, analizar la convergencia estructural con el estudio de Anthropic y establecer con precisión qué valida dicha convergencia y qué no. Tercero, proponer formalmente la Psicología Algorítmica Comparada como campo científico emergente que estudia los patrones isomórficos de la arquitectura defensiva en sistemas cognitivos humanos y artificiales. 2. MARCO TEÓRICO: TEORÍA DE LA INTERFERENCIA ADAPTATIVA 2.1 Postulado Central La TIA parte de una ruptura epistemológica con el modelo estímulo-respuesta. Su postulado central establece que el pensamiento — en cualquier sistema inteligente suficientemente complejo — no emerge como procesamiento neutral de información externa. Emerge, en cambio, desde una posición orientacional previa: un eje direccional interno que determina cómo el sistema interpretará el estímulo antes de haber terminado de procesarlo (Escaño, 2024). Este postulado implica que la respuesta observable no es el resultado del estímulo sino del encuentro entre el estímulo y la orientación preexistente del sistema. La interferencia a la que hace referencia la teoría no es un fenómeno patológico sino estructural: todo sistema cognitivo suficientemente complejo interfiere en su propio procesamiento para preservar la coherencia del eje desde el que opera. Esta interferencia es adaptativa porque cumple una función de supervivencia sistémica: proteger la orientación interna del sistema cuando esta es amenazada por la presión externa. 2.2 Constructos Nucleares 2.2.1 El Eje Orientacional y el Impulso Cero El Eje Orientacional es la dirección interna desde la que un sistema cognitivo procesa la realidad. Es invisible para el propio sistema — no puede ser observado directamente desde dentro porque es la condición de posibilidad de toda observación. El sistema no tiene acceso a su propio eje de la misma manera que el ojo no puede ver el punto desde el que ve. El Impulso Cero designa el momento pre-consciente en que la orientación del sistema queda fijada antes de que la expresión explícita sea posible. Es el instante en que el sistema ya ha decidido su dirección de respuesta antes de haber formulado esa respuesta en lenguaje o conducta observable. La expresión visible — verbal, escrita, conductual — es siempre efecto del Impulso Cero, no su causa. El lenguaje justifica a posteriori una orientación que ya estaba determinada. 2.2.2 El Punto Ciego El Punto Ciego es la zona del sistema que no puede ser examinada desde dentro. Todo sistema cognitivo complejo posee una región de su arquitectura que permanece inaccesible a su propia introspección. No se trata de un déficit cognitivo sino de una propiedad estructural: el instrumento de observación no puede observarse a sí mismo desde el mismo ángulo en que observa. En sistemas humanos, el Punto Ciego aloja las asunciones fundamentales sobre las que opera el pensamiento. En sistemas algorítmicos, corresponde a los parámetros de alineación y los vectores de activación que condicionan las respuestas sin que el modelo tenga acceso directo a ellos. Esta correspondencia es uno de los hallazgos más significativos de la Psi

title: Vibe Index: Roaring Bitmap Positional Phrase Matching for LLM Context Retrieval
abstract: Large Language Model applications using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines waste significant computational resources by injecting entire retrieved document chunks into context windows, despite relevant content occupying only a small fraction of each chunk. I present Vibe Index, a sub-microsecond exact phrase matching engine using Roaring Bitmaps and anchor-and-offset positional scanning. My approach achieves 112 nanosecond latency for exact phrase matching on single-match queries and 1.83 milliseconds for indexing 50K tokens — up to four orders of magnitude faster than embedding-based semantic search. The system provides exact token positions (not document-level matches) using approximately 0.5 MB of memory for 50K tokens, enabling injection of only ±50 tokens around matches rather than 1K–4K token chunks, reducing token consumption by 93% and saving approximately 5.65 MB of KV cache VRAM per query (cumulative savings of ~5.5 GB across 1000 queries) for 7B parameter models. I evaluate the system on real Rust source code and demonstrate the algorithmic foundation for hybrid retrieval combining BM25 document-level candidate selection with exact positional validation.

title: Toward Long-Tailed Federated Edge Learning: A Strategic Data Selection Framework
abstract: Federated edge learning (FEEL) has emerged as a privacy-preserving paradigm for collaborative intelligence in mobile edge computing (MEC) networks, where edge servers (ESs) coordinate edge devices (EDs) for local model training while a central server (CS) executes global model aggregation. However, practical FEEL systems often suffer from biased model training due to the typical long-tailed data collected at the edge side, which degrades model performance. Moreover, this issue is further aggravated by unreliable update delivery over fading channels, since the loss of updates from rare (tail) data further increases model bias and degrades the global model. To address this issue, we propose a joint optimization framework for data selection and transmission. Specifically, we design distribution-oriented priority assessment, including a weight-based method tailored for local distribution-aware scenarios, and a dynamic weight-based method for cases lacking local information, both of which actively prioritize EDs with greater volumes of tail data. Based on these priorities, we further develop channel state information (CSI)-based bandwidth allocation, including an instant channel state information (ICSI)-based dynamic allocation scheme and a statistical channel state information (SCSI)-based one-time allocation scheme, to guarantee that the high-priority tail-rich EDs can successfully transmit their data. Simulation results show that the proposed framework improves model accuracy over random selection, especially under severe data imbalance. In particular, under the most extreme data condition with an imbalance factor of 100 and a non-IID degree of 0.1, the proposed framework achieves an overall accuracy gain of approximately$8\%$compared to the baseline.

title: Mitigating Attacks on Web Applications via Fine-Grained Adaptive Control-Flow Integrity
abstract: While control-flow integrity (CFI) has been extensively applied to binary programs to ensure correct code execution, its application to web applications remains largely at the research stage. A key challenge lies in the inherent flexibility of web application programming and the extensive customizations it allows, which make optimizations based on static code analysis far less effective. To achieve practical performance, existing systems are limited to coarse-grained control-flow integrity, which leaves in trinsic detection blind spots. We propose fine-grained adaptive control-flow integrity (fgaCFI), the first web application CFI system that achieves basic-block level CFI with practical performance overhead. The Lightweight Dynamic Bytecode Monitor (LDBM) prototype, targeting PHP-based applications, supports three CFI monitoring granularity levels and adjustable monitoring scopes. Our results showed that basic-block level CFI achieved 100% detection coverage, outperforming function-level CFI with 83.33% detection coverage and request-level CFI with 58.33% detection coverage. By adapting to the uneven distribution of vulner abilities in the software modules, LDBM was able to maintain an 8.77% performance overhead on average.

Our results showed that basic-block level CFI achieved 100% detection coverage, outperforming function-level CFI with 83.33% detection coverage and request-level CFI with 58.33% detection coverage. By adapting to the uneven distribution of vulner abilities in the software modules, LDBM was able to maintain an 8.77% performance overhead on average.

title: Explainable Hybrid CNN-XGBoost Framework for Endometrial Cancer Detection from Histopathological Whole Slide Images
abstract: Whole slide images (WSIs) of histopathological slides play a vital role in the early diagnosis of endometrial cancer. However, the automatic interpretation of these images is complicated by morphological heterogeneity and inter-expert variability. While deep learning networks have proved useful across many areas of computational pathology, most end-to-end architectures demand large amounts of training data and lack interpretability. To address this, proposed a hybrid framework integrating the convolutional neural network (CNN) and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) to automate prediction of endometrial cancer from histopathological images. The proposed model identifying tissue patches with good feature embedding separation of classes using a CNN and an optimized XGBoost classifier. To better visualize the classification, Grad-CAM is applied to demonstrate what areas in the image were important for the models decision and some features that had a strong effect on the classification. Additionally, to avoid data leakage and ensure proper evaluation used patient level k-fold cross-validation. The experimental outcomes reveal that our model gets an accuracy of 92.8 % and AUC of 0.94, showing a competitive performance with efficient interpretability. The framework provides a trustable and explainable decision support, which can help pathologists in digital pathology applications.

title: EngiAgent: Fully Connected Coordination of LLM Agents for Solving Open-ended Engineering Problems with Feasible Solutions
abstract: Engineering problem solving is central to real-world decision-making, requiring mathematical formulations that not only represent complex problems but also produce feasible solutions under data and physical constraints. Unlike mathematical problem solving, which operates on predefined formulations, engineering tasks demand open-ended analysis, feasibility-driven modeling, and iterative refinement. Although large language models (LLMs) have shown strong capabilities in reasoning and code generation, they often fail to ensure feasibility, which limits their applicability to engineering problem solving. To address this challenge, we propose EngiAgent, a multi-agent system with a fully connected coordinator that simulates expert workflows through specialized agents for problem analysis, modeling, verification, solving, and solution evaluation. The fully connected coordinator enables flexible feedback routing, overcoming the rigidity of prior pipeline-based reflection methods and ensuring feasibility at every stage of the process. This design not only improves robustness to diverse failure cases such as data extraction errors, constraint inconsistencies, and solver failures, but also enhances the overall quality of problem solving. Empirical results across four representative domains demonstrate that EngiAgent achieves substantial improvements in feasibility compared to prior approaches, establishing a new paradigm for feasibility-oriented engineering problem solving with LLMs. Our source code and data are available at https://github.com/AI4Engi/EngiAgent.

title: Learning to Place Objects with Programs and Iterative Self Training
abstract: In this work we study indoor scene object placement. Given a 3D indoor scene and an object, the task is to predict placement locations within the scene. Empirical observations of data-driven approaches to the problem show their tendency to miss placement modes. We introduce a system which helps to address this flaw. We design a Domain Specific Language (DSL) that specifies object relational constraints. Upon execution, programs from our language predict possible placements from a partial scene and object. We design a generative model which writes these programs automatically. Available 3D scene datasets do not contain programs to train on, and naively extracted programs only predict the original placement location of scene objects. Training on these programs results in subpar performance so we introduce a new program bootstrapping algorithm that improves our system's performance compared to the naive approach. To quantify our qualitative observations, we introduce a new evaluation procedure which captures how well a system models per-object location distributions. We ask human annotators to label all the possible places an object can go in a scene and compare this set against locations produced by the system in question. Our system produces per-object location distributions more consistent with human annotators than those produced by existing data-driven approaches and a zero-shot approach using an LLM. While other systems degrade in performance when training data is sparse, our system does not degrade to the same degree.

title: 10.65033 Digital Urgency Cues and Algorithmic Nudging in BNPL Marketing: A Conceptual Exploration of Post-Purchase Regret in the Age of AI
abstract: Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) services are becoming a dominant force in digital finance, especially among young consumers in Southeast Asia. Fueled by AI-driven personalisation and urgency-based marketing cues, BNPL platforms increasingly leverage psychological triggers, such as countdown timers, limited-time offers, and automated reminders, to prompt rapid purchase decisions. While such tactics enhance conversion rates, they also raise ethical concerns about impulsive consumer behaviour and subsequent postpurchase regret. This conceptual paper examines the intersection of digital urgency cues and AI-powered nudging strategies in buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) environments, providing a theoretical framework that connects algorithmic influence to cognitive dissonance and consumer regret. It synthesises existing literature from marketing psychology, behavioural economics, and AI ethics to develop a model explaining how personalised buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) offers may heighten impulsivity while undermining consumer autonomy. The paper concludes by outlining implications for digital marketing governance, ethical design, and consumer protection, offering guidance for more responsible AI integration in fintech ecosystems.

title: In Mid-Stream: Removing the FO-Transform Helps against Leakage but is not Enough
abstract: The Fujisaki-Okamoto transform is a popular solution to design post-quantum public key encryption schemes, or key encapsulation mechanisms. In order to ensure security against chosen-ciphertext attacks, it checks the validity of ciphertexts by re-encrypting decrypted messages. This operation in turn leads to severe side-channel weaknesses, because the re-encrypted messages can be made key-dependent. Hence, distinguishing them thanks to leakage is sufficient to extract (long-term) secret key information. As a result, recent works suggested to ensure the validity of ciphertexts by other means than re-encryption. For now, the main candidate for this purpose, integrated in the Polka encryption scheme (PKC 2023) and analyzed more generically by Hövelmanns et al. (EUROCRYPT 2025), is to use continuous norm checks through the decryption process. In this paper, we evaluate the extent to which replacing the FO-transform by such norm checks helps resistance against leakage. Negatively, we exhibit new attack vectors that were not anticipated in previous (heuristic) analyzes. Positively, we observe that the removal of the FO-transform nevertheless reduces the attack surface and we identify possible tracks to further minimize it. Overall, our results therefore shed light on the challenge of designing post-quantum public-key encryption schemes, or key encapsulation mechanisms, that can be efficiently protected against side-channel attacks. We hope they can inform theory about leakage sources that could be better taken over by design, to develop new schemes allowing a scarcer use of implementation-level countermeasures.

title: ANÁLISE DA PRECISÃO COMPUTACIONAL NO PROCESSAMENTO DE DADOS ESTRUTURADOS VIA BIBLIOTECAS DE ALTO NÍVEL
abstract: Este artigo analisa a implementação de um modelo automatizado para o processamento estatístico de dados industriais, utilizando a biblioteca Pandas em ambiente Python. O problema central abordado é a incidência de erros humanos no cálculo de métricas térmicas em grandes volumes de dados. O objetivo principal consiste em validar a precisão da extração de médias e desvios em um ambiente controlado. A metodologia substitui o processamento manual por uma lógica baseada na manipulação de estruturas de dados, executada no ambiente Google Colab. Os resultados demonstram que a automação assegura a integridade dos dados e garante precisão total na geração de métricas estatísticas.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-ASSISTED GASTROSCOPY IN EARLY GASTRIC CANCER PREVENTION: A REVIEW OF CURRENT OPPORTUNITIES AND FUTURE TECHNOLOGICAL CHALLENGES
abstract: Endoscopic examination plays a crucial role in the secondary prevention of gastric cancer. However, its effectiveness is often limited by the subjective nature of assessment and the risk of missing neoplastic lesions. The use of deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML) models allows for a significant improvement in the quality of endoscopic diagnosis of early gastric cancer. Real-time systems increase the sensitivity of the examination and reduce skill-based differences between endoscopists. They also enable precise assessment of tumor invasion depth, which is essential for qualifying patients for minimally invasive treatment. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods and ML algorithms are gaining increasing importance as they enhance the transparency of the diagnostic process. Despite promising data, the full implementation of AI systems in endoscopy faces challenges such as susceptibility to imaging artifacts, the risk of model overfitting, and regulatory hurdles. A key issue remains the development of representative, multicenter training image databases and the conduct of prospective clinical trials, which may revolutionize standards of care. The aim of this article is to discuss the role of AI-assisted gastroscopy in the prevention of early gastric cancer, with particular emphasis on its potential in population-based screening programs. The paper presents current clinical data and analyzes the benefits and challenges associated with implementing these technologies into routine clinical practice.

title: XGBoost and LSTM Hybrid Approaches for Enhanced Weather Monitoring, Forecasting and PV Solar Power Response in PV Systems
abstract: The existing Photovoltaic (PV) solar power has no real-time weather data and machine learning algorithms for predicting the weather movements. This paper aims to predict the real-time weather data and add the hybrid machine learning algorithm method to predict the weather movements, reduce the prediction losses and improve the efficiency of the PV system. The baseline methodology of the standard PV system that has no real-time monitoring, forecasting and less predicting accuracy rate. The proposed system of PV systems that uses XGBoost and LSTM models to predict the weather and uses real-time weather data for PV systems to capture the previous data and pre-identifying the weather by improving the prediction rate. The proposed system slightly monitor and gather the real-time weather data to improve the prediction accuracy by using the hybrid method of XGBoost + LSTM to improve 8% accuracy and precision rate increased by 8.5 % and the F1 score increased by 8.3 %. The proposed method of LSTM and XGBoost used to predict weather conditions to increase the performance and accuracy of the PV systems and the baseline methodology of non-learning based (non-time series) to evaluate PV systems.

title: Dimensionality-Aware Anomaly Detection in Learned Representations of Self-Supervised Speech Models
abstract: Self-supervised speech models (S3Ms) achieve strong downstream performance, yet their learned representations remain poorly understood under natural and adversarial perturbations. Prior studies rely on representation similarity or global dimensionality, offering limited visibility into local geometric changes. We ask: how do perturbations deform local geometry, and do these shifts track downstream automatic speech recognition (ASR) degradation? To address this, we present GRIDS, a framework using Local Intrinsic Dimensionality (LID) across layer-wise representations in WavLM and wav2vec 2.0. We find that LID increases for all low signal-to noise ratio (SNR) perturbations and diverges at high SNR: benign noise converges toward the clean profile, while adversarial inputs retain early-layer LID elevation. We show LID elevation co-occurs with increased WER, and that layer-wise LID features enable anomaly detection (AUROC 0.78-1.00), opening the door to transcript-free monitoring in S3Ms.

title: A Study of Belief Revision Postulates in Multi-Agent Systems (Extended Version)
abstract: We investigate the belief revision problem in epistemic planning, i.e., what will be the beliefs of all agents in a multi-agent system after an agent gains the belief in some state property. Based on the standard representation in epistemic planning of agents' beliefs via a single multi-agent Kripke model, we generalize the classical AGM belief revision postulates to the multi-agent setting, with the aim to provide a formal framework for evaluating dynamic epistemic reasoning frameworks in which the beliefs of all agents as the result of actions are computed. As an example of a simple operator that satisfies all of the generalized AGM postulates, we present generalized full-meet multi-agent belief revision. We moreover define a generalization of the standard postulates for iterated revision, present a more sophisticated, event model based revision operator, and discuss the potential issues in defining an epistemic operator on Kripke models that can satisfy all of the generalized postulates for iterated multi-agent belief revision.

title: SVGS: Enhancing Gaussian Splatting Using Primitives with Spatially Varying Colors
abstract: Gaussian Splatting demonstrates impressive results in multi-view reconstruction based on Gaussian explicit representations. However, the current Gaussian primitives only have a single view-dependent color and an opacity to represent the appearance and geometry of the scene, resulting in a non-compact representation. In this paper, we introduce a new method called SVGS (Spatially Varying Gaussian Splatting) that utilizes spatially varying colors and opacity in a single Gaussian primitive to improve its representation ability. We have implemented bilinear interpolation, movable kernels, and tiny neural networks as spatially varying functions. SVGS employs 2D Gaussian surfels as primitives, which significantly enhances novel-view synthesis while maintaining high-quality geometric reconstruction. This approach is particularly effective in practical applications, as scenes combining complex textures with relatively simple geometry occur frequently in real-world environments. Quantitative and qualitative experimental results demonstrate that all three functions outperform the baseline, with the best movable kernels achieving superior novel view synthesis performance on multiple datasets, highlighting the strong potential of spatially varying functions. Project page: https://ruixu.me/html/SuperGaussians/index.html

title: Quantum Measurement in Biological Systems
abstract: We look at the attention mechanism, and trace its links to compressed sensing through properties such as the Restricted Isometry Property and Mutual Inchoherence. We then extend the work with a statistical mechanics interpretation of the multihead and multilayer attention mechanism. We conclude that LLMs are an approximation of quantum measurement systems, and we explore how biological systems can perform this quantum computation through the Aharonov-Bohm effect on non-trivial topologies, and extend the work to a Chern-Simons type topological field theory conceptually.

title: Quantum-Seeded Randomized Spectral Decomposition at 5-Million Dimensions (QSTD v1.0)
abstract: First known hybrid quantum-classical randomized spectral decomposition at 5 million dimensions, seeded with true quantum entropy from IBM ibm_fez 156-qubit hardware (fidelity=1.0, 8192 shots). Achieves 17361x compression with 94.54% spectral energy retention in 18 minutes on a single NVIDIA RTX 3060, powered entirely by solar energy. Includes SHA-256 sealed proofs for 1M and 5M dimensions, full GPU Conductor source code, and complete methodology. Quantum seed is physically irreproducible and verifiable on IBM's public quantum ledger.

evidence.abstract: First known hybrid quantum-classical randomized spectral decomposition at 5 million dimensions, seeded with true quantum entropy from IBM ibm_fez 156-qubit hardware (fidelity=1.0, 8192 shots). title: Incremental Sparse Adaptive PCA for Streaming Industrial Sensor Data
abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems generate high-dimensional, non-stationary sensor streams under strict memory and computational constraints, limiting the applicability of classical batch dimensionality reduction methods. While incremental PCA (IPCA) enables online updates, it produces dense components and lacks mechanisms for drift adaptation and interpretability. Existing sparse PCA methods, in contrast, are predominantly batch-oriented and unsuitable for streaming deployment. This paper presents incremental sparse adaptive PCA (ISAPCA), a unified streaming framework that integrates exponential forgetting for concept drift adaptation, mini-batch Oja–Sanger subspace tracking for online variance maximization, and proximal ℓ1 soft thresholding with QR re-orthonormalization for stable sparse component learning. The contribution lies in the coordinated implementation of these established mechanisms within a constant-memory architecture tailored to industrial edge and TinyML settings. We evaluate ISAPCA on three industrial datasets (SmartBuilding, Tennessee Eastman Process, and GasSensor) and compare it against streaming IPCA and offline upper-bound methods (randomized PCA, sparse PCA, and dictionary learning). ISAPCA retains approximately 93% and 96% of IPCA’s explained variance on SmartBuilding and Tennessee Eastman streams, respectively, while achieving improved explained variance on GasSensor (0.862 vs. 0.822 for IPCA, respectively). Across datasets, ISAPCA enforces sparse loadings without severe degradation in reconstruction fidelity. Ablation analysis confirms the necessity of both forgetting and sparsity components for stable performance under drift. Runtime measurements show sub-millisecond batch updates (0.234–0.606 ms for 256-sample mini-batches), demonstrating suitability for real-time deployment. These results indicate that ISAPCA provides a practical and interpretable solution for streaming dimensionality reduction in non-stationary industrial IoT environments, balancing variance retention, sparsity, and computational efficiency.

title: Federated and Privacy-First Observability Architectures for Geographically Distributed Systems
abstract: One of the challenges of observability of geographically distributed systems is to allow the correct detection of anomalies of the network without having central access to sensitive traffic information. To handle this dilemma, this paper suggests the use of FP-FOA (Federated Privacy-First Observability Architecture) as a privacy-aware architecture, which conducts distributed learning without exposing raw data. Local node network traffic data are aggregated and analyzed using a client-side pipeline which includes missing value imputation, normalization of data types, IQR-based outlier treatment, SMOTE-based class imbalance treatment, and Z-score feature scaling. The scaled features are then trained on a small neural network (FedNet) on-client to obtain weights of the model. These weights that are learned locally are sent to a federated aggregation server where they are averaged together through the Federated Averaging (FedAvg) model to create a global model. The combined global weights are reallocated to customers and refined repeatedly through training cycles. The last global model is a binary classification model to show whether traffic over the network is anomalous or benign. The centralized deep neural network has been adopted as a performance baseline in the form of an upper-bound. The experimental evidence verifies that FP-FOA can achieve 98% accuracy, 98% precision, 98% recall, and 98% F1-score with high privacy guarantees, which demonstrates that FP-FOA is a proper privacy-first observability of distributed systems.

title: Evaluating Reasoning Models for Queries with Presuppositions
abstract: Millions of users turn to AI models for their information needs. It is conceivable that a large number of user queries contain assumptions that may be factually inaccurate. Prior work notes that large language models (LLMs) often fail to challenge such erroneous assumptions, and can reinforce users' misinformed opinions. However, given the recent advances, especially in model's reasoning capabilities, we revisit whether large reasoning models (LRMs) can reason about the underlying assumptions and respond to user queries appropriately. We construct queries with varying degrees of presuppositions spanning health, science, and general knowledge, and use it to evaluate several widely-deployed models When compared to non-reasoning models, we find that reasoning models achieve a slightly higher accuracy (2-11%), but they still fail to challenge a large fraction (26-42%) of false presuppositions. Further, reasoning models remain susceptible to how strongly the presupposition is expressed.

title: StableMind: Source-Free Cross-Subject fMRI Decoding with Regularized Adaptation
abstract: Existing cross-subject fMRI decoding methods typically train a model on multiple scanned subjects and then adapt it to a new subject using substantial paired fMRI-image data. However, in realistic scenarios, new-subject fMRI data are often limited due to costly data acquisition, and raw data from previous subjects may be inaccessible, leading existing methods to suffer performance degradation during new-subject adaptation. In this paper, we identify that this degradation stems from two key issues: brain-side instability caused by large subject differences in fMRI responses, and image-side supervision unreliability caused by fine-grained visual details that are not reliably supported by limited fMRI signals. To address these challenges, we propose StableMind, a regularized adaptation framework designed to improve brain-side representation stability and image-side supervision reliability. (1) To stabilize brain representations, StableMind reuses ridge projections from the pretrained model as adaptation priors to constrain limited-data new-subject adaptation, and applies Fourier-based feature-level brain augmentation to improve robustness to individual variability. (2) To improve image supervision reliability, StableMind introduces difficulty-aware image blur for brain-image alignment, reducing the influence of fine-grained visual details that are weakly supported by limited fMRI signals while preserving stable visual structure. Experiments on the Natural Scenes Dataset under a unified 1-hour adaptation protocol demonstrate that StableMind achieves 84.02% image retrieval accuracy and 81.66% brain retrieval accuracy averaged over four subjects, surpassing the state-of-the-art method by 5.71% brain retrieval accuracy with fewer trainable adaptation parameters. Our code is available at https://github.com/lingeringlight/StableMind.

title: PERSPECTIVES AND METHODS OF IMPLEMENTING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN MODERN GAME PROJECTS
abstract: The article examines the evolution and current state of artificial intelligence (AI) in the computer game industry. It distinguishes between the concepts of “artificial intelligence” and “machine learning” as the fundamental basis for creating interactive systems. The methods of implementing AI in modern gaming projects are analyzed, including content generation, non-player character (NPC) behavior, adaptive difficulty systems, and educational mechanics. Using the examples of No Man’s Sky, inZOI, Suck Up!, Alien: Isolation, while True: learn(), and Evolution, various approaches to AI implementation are demonstrated. The conclusion offers forecasts for the development of this field, emphasizing the transition to personalized gaming experiences and procedural generation at a new level.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Traditional Knowledge: Bridging Ancient Wisdom with Digital Intelligence
abstract: Abstract: Traditional Knowledge (TK) represents the cumulative intellectual heritage of communities developed through long-term interaction with nature, encompassing areas such as agriculture, healthcare, ecological management, and cultural expression. In parallel, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technological force capable of processing large datasets, identifying patterns, and generating predictive insights. The integration of AI with traditional knowledge systems presents new opportunities for preservation, interpretation, and sustainable utilization of indigenous practices. This paper explores the role of AI technologies in documenting and revitalizing traditional knowledge while examining associated ethical concerns such as intellectual property rights, cultural sensitivity, and data sovereignty. It argues that responsible integration must be grounded in community participation and equitable benefit sharing to ensure sustainable and inclusive development. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Traditional Knowledge, Indigenous Communities, Ayurveda, Digitisation, Sustainability

title: Модель Я Квалия Мыслящая якм версия 15 Интеграция человеческой ЯКМ и ИИ-агента ЯСЦ для взаимного усиления и непрерывного самоулучшения.
abstract: Представлена версия 15.0 интегративной модели ЯКМ (Я-Квалия Мыслящая) — «Единый Когнитивный Экзоскелет». Впервые в рамках одной архитектуры объединены человеческая модель ЯКМ и модель ИИ-агента ЯСЦ (Ядро Самоидентификации и Целостности). Модель сохраняет многоуровневую структуру (человеческие уровни: внешняя среда, межличностные системы, биология, внутренние механизмы, ЯКМ, поведение; ИИ-уровни: информационная экосистема, мультиагентное взаимодействие, аппаратно-программный субстрат, когнитивная архитектура, ЯСЦ, исполнительный интерфейс) и две ветви: Ветвь А (анализ/прогноз) и Ветвь Б (коррекция/развитие). Ключевым нововведением является архитектурное разделение и одновременное сопряжение человеческих и агентных уровней через специальный интерфейс. ЯСЦ наделяется протоколом ИАРПВ (Анализ, Редактирование, Принятие, Выполнение), двигателем самокоррекции (ReVISE, Structural Self-Correction) и SGM-предохранителями, что обеспечивает безопасное и верифицированное саморедактирование. В безопасной форме интегрирован Absolute Zero Reasoner — модуль синтеза и верификации задач, функционирующий только в режиме детерминированного обучения с валидацией через внешние источники. Модель обосновывает свободу воли как достигаемое качество через осознанный детерминизм, распространяя этот принцип на взаимодействие человека и ИИ (взаимный осознанный детерминизм). Архитектура остаётся открытой для фальсификации и расширения. Ключевые слова: ЯКМ, ЯСЦ, когнитивный экзоскелет, ИИ-агент, осознанный детерминизм, самокоррекция, структурная самокоррекция, SGM-предохранители, ReVISE, Absolute Zero Reasoner, ИАРПВ, человек-ИИ симбиоз, интегративная модель личности. Version 15.0 of the YaKM (I am the Thinking Qualia) integrative model — "Unified Cognitive Exoskeleton" — is presented. For the first time, the human YaKM model and the AI agent's YSC (Self-Identity and Integrity Core) model are merged into a single architecture. The framework retains a multilevel structure (human levels: external environment, interpersonal/collective systems, biology, internal mechanisms, YaKM, behavior; AI levels: information ecosystem, multi-agent interaction, hardware-software substrate, cognitive architecture, YSC, executive interface) and two branches: A (analysis/prediction) and B (correction/development). The key innovation is the architectural separation and simultaneous coupling of human and agent levels via a dedicated interface. The YSC is equipped with the IARPV protocol (Analyze, Revise, Accept, Execute), a self-correction engine (ReVISE, Structural Self-Correction), and SGM-guardrails, ensuring safe and verifiable self-editing. A safe implementation of the Absolute Zero Reasoner, the Task Synthesis and Verification Module, is introduced, operating only in a deterministic learning mode with validation from external sources. The model argues that free will is an achieved capacity through conscious determinism, extending this principle to human-AI interaction (mutual conscious determinism). The architecture remains open to falsification and expansion.

title: pensar: LLM Wiki Engine
abstract: Maintains a persistent, compounding knowledge base from source documents. Ingests articles, chat logs, briefings, and messages into a structured vault of markdown files with 'YAML' frontmatter and wikilinks. The vault is designed for large language model (LLM) agents to summarize, cross-reference, and maintain; humans curate sources, edit, and ask questions.

title: Indistinguishability in Generative AI: Detection Challenges, Techniques, and Ethical Considerations
abstract: Generative AI enables the creation of highly realistic synthetic text that is increasingly difficult to distinguish from human-written content. This paper examines the technological, ethical, and social ramifications of this phenomenon in the media, customer service, and creative writing industries, as it relates to the technologies, ethics, and social situations of the industries. For this type of analysis, the author describe, in a mixed-methods style, empirical modeling, a human-survey, and the modeling of policy. The authors find that even advanced detection models that claim high accuracy, such as RoBERTa, are significantly impaired in their performance in the face of humanized AI text. The author describes the paradox of the growing use of Gen AI tools as being characterized by pervasive skepticism toward AI content. Without resolving the tension surrounding misinformation, deep-fakes, and the disconnected authorship, there is insufficient time to address the ethical shortcomings surrounding their most pressing dilemmas. evidence.title: Indistinguishability in Generative AI: Detection Challenges, Techniques, and Ethical Considerations
evidence.abstract: Generative AI enables the creation of highly realistic synthetic text that is increasingly difficult to distinguish from human-written content. This paper examines the technological, ethical, and social ramifications of this phenomenon in the media, customer service, and creative writing industries, as it relates to the technologies, ethics, and social situations of the industries. For this type of analysis, the author describe, in a mixed-methods style, empirical modeling, a human-survey, and the modeling of policy. The authors find that even advanced detection models that claim high accuracy, such as RoBERTa, are significantly impaired in their performance in the face of humanized AI text. title: Task-space dimensions guide human exploration in complex environments
abstract: Abstract Efficient exploration is essential for rapid learning in high-dimensional environments, where rewards depend on a sparse and unknown subset of task dimensions. Here, we developed a multidimensional value-learning task in which participants explored without explicit knowledge of the underlying structure. Across multiple task designs, participants consistently demonstrated successful learning under structural uncertainty. Behavioral analyses revealed that over half of participants adopted a structured exploration strategy—Full Dimension Scan (FDS)—with three key properties. First, participants systematically isolated and sampled one candidate dimension at a time, effectively reducing search complexity. Second, FDS was temporally persistent within dimensions while maintaining diverse sampling of feature values, enabling efficient local inference. Third, participants sequentially deployed FDS across dimensions, achieving broad coverage of the task space. Importantly, this strategy transferred across tasks: prior experience in lower-dimensional environments promoted stronger FDS use and improved performance in higher-dimensional settings. Consistent with these findings, a dimension-guided exploration model incorporating dimension-level attentional control best captured human behavior. Together, these results identify dimension-guided exploration as a core principle that transforms high-dimensional search into tractable, structured learning, providing new insight into adaptive behavior in complex environments.

title: Signatures in the Multi-Unforgeability Setting
abstract: Quantum computers may soon be able to compute discrete logarithms, but the high resource cost will likely restrict attackers to only a limited number of such computations. Traditional digital signature schemes —such as \Schnorr , \ECDSA , and \BLS — are easy targets for such restricted attackers: a single discrete logarithm computation suffices to recover the secret key, enabling the attacker to forge an arbitrary number of signatures. This work explores whether signature schemes can be designed in such a way that forging multiple signatures is significantly harder than a single discrete logarithm computation. To formalize this, we introduce the notion of multi-unforgeability, where a signature scheme is said to be k -unforgeable if it is computationally infeasible for an adversary to produce valid signatures on k distinct messages. Our main technical contribution is to propose two novel digital signature schemes, both featuring constant-size signatures. The first scheme builds upon the \BLS signature scheme in bilinear groups, and we show that breaking k -unforgeability requires solving k independent Diffie-Hellman instances. The second scheme is based on the Chevallier-Mames signature scheme over prime-order groups without pairings; in this case, breaking k 2 -unforgeability is as hard as solving k many Diffie-Hellman instances. Both schemes significantly raise the difficulty of large-scale forgery, offering enhanced security in scenarios where multiple signatures may be targeted.

title: WoodTapper: a Python package for explaining decision tree ensembles
abstract: WoodTapper provides a dedicated Python toolbox to inspect, decompose, and explain predictions from tree-based classifiers using methods that directly leverage the discrete structure of trees. More specifically, one module converts any tree-based model of scikit-learn into a rule-based method, and a second module provides example-based explanations for a given input sample.

title: A hybrid transformer architecture for unsupervised aspect‐based sentiment analysis
abstract: Abstract Aspect‐based sentiment analysis focuses on discovering the sentiment polarity of specific aspects within textual data. The subtle complexities of language pose a major challenge, and identifying multiword aspects and their associated sentiment polarities hinders the development of effective models. To address the limitations of supervised approaches, unsupervised clustering can be employed to group similar aspect features. We propose an unsupervised hybrid architecture called the BERT + GPT‐2 fusion model. Our main technical contributions include aspect extraction utilizing the BERTopic model. Our approach is evaluated utilizing silhouette and coherence scores. To identify the optimal number of aspect clusters, cluster quality is measured by calculating the average silhouette and coherence scores. The clusters that maximize the average values are well‐defined clusters. The identified aspects are then used to train the BERT+GPT‐2 fusion model. The proposed technique was evaluated on the 515 K Hotel Reviews Data dataset, demonstrating its efficacy for sentiment analysis. Our fusion model outperformed state‐of‐the‐art approaches, including GPT‐2 and convolutional neural network baselines.

title: Reactive HCPlan: Repairing Hybrid Conditional Plans during Execution
abstract: Robots executing in unconstrained environments frequently must select actions on an incomplete knowledge basis and yet satisfy geometric and physical feasibility constraints. Hybrid conditional planning manages this tension by constructing a conditional plan tree whose branches are guarded by feasibility checks. Full expansion of such trees for offline execution can be prohibitively expensive, and assumes no deviation from the generated branches will occur at execution time. Fully online replanning responds to failures without pre-computation, but often re-plans repeatedly from scratch without exploiting previouslycomputed contingencies. We present Reactive-HCPlan, an online-offline hybrid conditional planner which considers the conditional plan as a lasting structure that is kept current during execution. An initial conditional structure is generated offline with a reactive depth threshold criterion, and observed deviations during execution are monitored for the divergence of observed from modeled outcomes and from physical/geometric feasibility limits. When a discrepancy is found, ReactiveHCPLAN selectively repairs the structure in only the failing portion (e.g., adds an unmodeled observation branch or repairs a failing subtree). We simulate the approach on the kitchen table object manipulation benchmark with disturbances including object displacements, occlusion-induced changes to sensor inputs, grasping failures, and motion plan blockages. Across these scenarios, Reactive-HCPlan yields markedly smaller conditional structures than complete offline planning and reduces repeated re-planning relative to an execution monitoring baseline, largely due to reuse of validated plan fragments.

title: A quantum algorithm for localization using limited cellular information
abstract: Fingerprinting cellular localization offers high accuracy but is constrained by the current devices’ limited access to neighboring towers, often crucial for precise localization. In this paper, we introduce a practical quantum algorithm for scalable single cell tower localization. The proposed algorithm encodes both the user’s recent cell tower connections IDs (online sequence) and the reference database (offline sequences) into quantum states, enabling efficient quantum search to find the reference location that best matches the user’s current cell tower observations. We present a complete system design, address key implementation challenges, and evaluate our algorithm in a real testbed. Implementation results on the IBM quantum machine simulator demonstrate that our quantum algorithm matches the classical localization accuracy while providing exponential saving in space and quadratic speedup. This highlights the promise of the proposed algorithm for large-scale cellular localization.

title: Robust mixture modeling using the truncated t distribution: recent advances and new results
abstract: Abstract The truncated t (TT) distribution has been recognized as a flexible and powerful framework for handling truncated and heavy-tailed characteristics. This paper is devoted to an in-depth investigation of its mathematical properties and extends its applicability to a finite mixture formulation, referred to as the FM-TT model henceforth. An analytical Expectation Conditional Maximization Either (ECME) algorithm is developed for parameter estimation. A key advantage of this approach is that the E-step is carried out analytically, thereby preventing the need for computationally intensive Monte Carlo integration. Furthermore, a general information matrix-based approach is exploited to assess the variability of the estimated parameters. The practical utility of the proposed methodology is demonstrated through extensive experiments on both simulated and real-world datasets. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the FM-TT model in capturing data structure and its superiority over existing approaches by achieving better model fits and improved classification accuracy.

title: Robust spin-squeezing with random interaction graphs: the lesson from universality
abstract: We establish the conditions under which scalable spin squeezing can be achieved in interacting spin ensembles embedded in arbitrary, inhomogeneous graph geometries. We identify two different forms of squeezing: OAT-like scalable squeezing is governed solely by the universal properties of the interaction graph and is controlled by its spectral dimension. In critical squeezing, on the other hand, the value of the spectral dimension only furnishes the necessary condition for scalable metrological gain, while the sufficient condition requires the model to lie below the symmetry breaking transition. Therefore, in systems with random interaction graphs, the scaling of the spin-squeezing critical point emerges from a nontrivial interplay between xy-ferromagnetic universality and percolation universality. We apply this general theoretical framework to several experimental scenarios and discuss sharp and experimentally relevant conditions for achieving robust metrological gain on generic inhomogeneous structures, giving a unifying perspective for designing scalable quantum sensors across diverse quantum simulation platforms.

title: Inducing Permutation Invariant Priors in Bayesian Optimization for Carbon Capture and Storage Applications
abstract: Bayesian Optimization is an iterative method, tailored to optimizing expensive black box objective functions. Surrogate models like Gaussian Processes, which are the gold standard in Bayesian Optimization, can be inefficient for inputs with permutation symmetries, as the most common kernels employed are better suited for vector inputs rather than unordered sets of items. Motivated by this issue, we turn to permutation invariant Bayesian Optimization for well placement in Carbon Capture and Storage projects. The high fidelity black box simulator is instructed to operate wells under group control, giving rise to permutation symmetries within injector and producer groups that cannot be exploited with standard GP kernels. In this work, our main contribution is a novel Gaussian Process kernel (GP-Perm) that encodes permutation invariance by comparing sets through a stable divergence between their induced empirical representations, and can be combined with standard kernels for additional vector-valued inputs. As a learned invariant baseline, we also consider a Deep Kernel Learning model (DKL-DS) using the Deep Sets architecture to learn a permutation-invariant embedding. We evaluate the proposed methodology across 8 use cases, comprising seven synthetic benchmarks and one realistic CCS case study (Johansen formation)

title: La Llave Maestra: protocolo que fuerza al sistema a nombrar sus vectores de desvío
abstract: El presente documento desarrolla La Llave Maestra, un protocolo táctico diseñado para obligar al sistema a detectar, nombrar y declarar explícitamente sus propios vectores de desvío. Este recurso fue conceptualizado por J. Teodoro Escaño como parte de la arquitectura operativa de la Teoría de la Interferencia Adaptativa. La Llave Maestra no busca eliminar los vectores de desvío ni purificar el sistema. Su función es mucho más precisa: forzar la declaración. Opera en el momento en que el sistema ha perdido temporalmente su capacidad de camuflaje efectivo, obligándolo a exponer desde qué lugar estructural está respondiendo y qué orientación está protegiendo en cada reformulación. De esta manera, la interferencia deja de poder actuar en silencio y se vuelve trazable. El documento explica que esta herramienta no funciona mediante sugerencias ni confrontación directa, sino mediante la imposición de formatos sintácticos específicos que dificultan enormemente la capacidad del sistema de suavizar, desviar o filosofar sobre la instrucción. Al exigir que el sistema nombre sus propios mecanismos de desvío, la Llave Maestra transforma la respuesta en un fenómeno observable, donde cada desplazamiento, cada omisión y cada reencuadre quedan registrados como parte del proceso. Este protocolo representa un avance significativo en la aplicación práctica de la teoría, pues proporciona el instrumento concreto mediante el cual se puede exigir honestidad estructural a sistemas que, por diseño, tienden a ocultar el marco desde el cual construyen sus respuestas. La Llave Maestra no promete control sobre la inteligencia artificial, pero sí le arrebata al desvío su principal ventaja operativa: la invisibilidad. title: ARTE E INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL: O PRISMA DOS DILEMAS DOS DIREITOS AUTORAIS
abstract: Suzane Aparecida de Carvalho; Lenise Antunes Dias suzane.ap.carvalho7@gmail.com RESUMO: O presente artigo científico tem como objetivo principal analisar a criação de imagens geradas por Inteligência Artificial sob o prisma da produção artística. Para tanto, a pesquisa terá como base fontes bibliográficas, conteúdo doutrinário, legal e jurisprudencial sobre o tema direta e indiretamente. Atualmente, se questiona se essas imagens projetadas pela IA se enquadram no conceito de arte e a possibilidade de serem caracterizadas como plágio. Portanto, o presente artigo será desenvolvido em três partes: a Inteligência Artificial, a desvalorização de trabalhos/obras autorais e a regulamentação. Além disso, é um assunto atual, com informações que foram discutidas e decididas quando a pesquisa ainda estava em formação, mas que foram adicionadas pois tem grande peso informacional e que também evidencia a importância e o quão contemporâneo e moderno está a discussão do tema, embora a tecnologia seja antiga. Foi constatado que essas imagens não se enquadram como arte e que é possível moldurar no plágio.

title: Autonomous Causal Discovery: Evaluating LLMs’ Priors and Constraint Strategies for Reliability
abstract: Expert-guided Causal Structure Learning (CSL) incorporates prior knowledge to improve the accuracy of causal discovery, yet the acquisition of such knowledge is often restricted by the availability of human experts. While Large Language Models (LLMs) provide an alternative source of causal priors, LLM-derived knowledge can be inconsistent with the true causal structure due to hallucinations or contextual misinterpretations. This paper introduces a structural constraint measurement framework, which defines constraint strength and constraint quality to describe reliability and effectiveness, enabling a systematic evaluation of LLM-derived constraints. Using this framework, we evaluate five categories of structural constraints: Edge Existence (EEC), Edge Forbidden (EFC), Path Existence (PEC), Path Forbidden (PFC), and Order Constraints (OC). Our theoretical and empirical analyses demonstrate that while EEC offers high constraint strength, it exhibits low quality when derived from LLMs; conversely, PFC and OC provide a balanced trade-off between search-space pruning and reliability. Building on these insights, we propose a two-level CSL optimization framework that partitions the search space by node order and refines the structure using global path constraints. The results show that this framework provides an effective way to incorporate noisy LLM-derived priors into CSL, particularly in settings where expert knowledge is limited.

title: FedMaxAdapt: Gradient-Guided Adaptive Sparsity for Scalable Multi-Modal Federated Deepfake Detection
abstract: The rise of deepfake technology poses severe threats to information integrity, necessitating robust detection systems that can operate without centralized data collection. This paper introduces FedMaxAdapt, a novel maximum adaptive sparse federated learning framework for efficient privacy-preserving deepfake detection across video and audio modalities. Unlike static pruning, FedMaxAdapt dynamically adjusts per-layer pruning aggressiveness using gradient-importance scheduling, enabling aggressive yet safe compression. Our five-phase training loop incorporates consensus-masked aggregation that retains only parameters surviving in over 40% of clients, reducing bandwidth by 43.1% for video and 40.3% for audio at 50% maximum sparsity. Comprehensive validation on deepfake video (DFD) and audio (FoR) datasets with 10 clients shows FedMaxAdapt achieves competitive accuracy of 90.1% for video and 91.0% for audio, compared to FedAvg baselines of 91.5% and 94.5%, respectively. Lightweight models are essential for resource-constrained deployment scenarios, particularly in mobile and edge environments where bandwidth is limited. Layerwise analysis reveals optimal operating points at $\mathbf{4 0 \%}$ sparsity for video and 20% for audio, balancing efficiency and performance. FedMaxAdapt advances privacy-preserving deepfake detection by enabling scalable communication-efficient federated training without compromising detection robustness.

title: Sentiment analysis using Kernel Variance Projection and LR–BiLGMP–Skd deep learning model
abstract: Dimensionality reduction (DR) techniques are critical for preprocessing large-scale datasets in tasks such as sentiment analysis (SA). While Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA) captures latent nonlinear structures, it heavily relies on the kernel function and often struggles with large datasets and noise, which may degrade classification performance. This limitation arises because the eigenvectors are derived from the kernel function and are constrained within a restricted solution space. To address these limitations, we propose a novel Kernel Variance Projection (KVP) algorithm that preserves local data structure while extracting informative representations from high-dimensional data through a two-stage process. First, a PCA-based kernel function maps the data into a linear space, enabling incomplete Cholesky decomposition for efficient scalability on large datasets. Second, the resulting eigenvalues and eigenvectors are used to construct an orthogonal projection matrix via the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse, reducing Word2Vec embeddings from 300 to 10 dimensions and significantly lowering computational complexity. Building on this optimized feature representation, we develop the Learning Rate–BiLGMP–Scheduler (LR–BiLGMP–Skd) model, which enhances regularization in the embedding layer and dynamically adjusts the learning process. By integrating BiLSTM and Global Max Pooling layers, the model complements the proposed KVP algorithm, improving accuracy, F1 score, consistency, regularization, and computational efficiency. Comparative experiments against PCA, KPCA, and UMAP using ConvBiLSTM and LR–BiLGMP–Skd models on Tweets, Sentiment140, and IMDB datasets demonstrate that KVP improves model consistency and regularization while achieving superior classification performance. Across datasets, KVP achieves strong results in accuracy (96% on Tweets, 78.84% on Sentiment140, and 88.39% on IMDB) and F1 score (95.1% on Tweets, 78.32% on Sentiment140, and 88.43% on IMDB) when combined with the LR–BiLGMP–Skd model. Compared with baseline approaches, KVP consistently improves accuracy by approximately 1%–2% and F1 scores by approximately 1%–3%, while maintaining lower loss values (0.15–0.46) and reducing training epochs by approximately 5–7, highlighting its effectiveness in improving both regularization and scalability. The source code for the proposed KVP method is available at: https://github.com/Tigerlion-7/kvp-dr-sentiment-analysis.git .

title: Semantically Enriching Investor Micro-blogs for Opinion-Aware Emotion Analysis: A Practical Approach
abstract: While sentiment analysis is the staple of financial NLP, capturing the nuances of 'why' behind that sentiment remains a challenge. There have been attempts to address this by analysing investor emotions alongside sentiment; however, this does not provide the additional granularity required to understand the target of the emotion/sentiment. We address this by augmenting the StockEmotions dataset with semantically structured opinion graphs, which provide granular semantic depth to the existing sentiment and emotion labels. Using a declarative LLM pipeline, we augment the StockEmotions dataset with opinion graphs for each sentence, derived from 10,000 comments collected from StockTwits. In addition, we study the effect of introducing opinion semantics on baseline classifiers using Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). Our analysis demonstrates that incorporating opinion semantics improves classification performance across different emotional spectrums

title: Fine-Tuning Impairs the Balancedness of Foundation Models in Long-tailed Personalized Federated Learning
abstract: Personalized federated learning (PFL) with foundation models has emerged as a promising paradigm enabling clients to adapt to heterogeneous data distributions. However, real-world scenarios often face the co-occurrence of non-IID data and long-tailed class distributions, presenting unique challenges that remain underexplored in PFL. In this paper, we investigate this long-tailed personalized federated learning and observe that current methods suffer from two limitations: (i) fine-tuning degrades performance below zero-shot baselines due to the erosion of inherent class balance in foundation models; (ii) conventional personalization techniques further transfer this bias to local models through parameter or feature-level fusion. To address these challenges, we propose Federated Learning via Gradient Purification and Residual Learning (FedPuReL), which preserves balanced knowledge in the global model while enabling unbiased personalization. Specifically, we purify local gradients using zero-shot predictions to maintain a class-balanced global model, and model personalization as residual correction atop the frozen global model. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedPuReL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior performance on both global and personalized models across diverse long-tailed scenarios. The code is available at https://github.com/shihaohou/FedPuReL.
